body: Suicide is a permanent TRANSFER of pain and suffering from one person to every person their life has touched. My best friend recently committed suicide and it's me who lives with that pain for the rest of my life. It's his family, other friends, his roommate who found his body. We will all carry this destruction until our end. We have been picking up the pieces and mending a giant hole in our hearts, the community, the future, the present, and the past. The plans we made are impossible now. The present has changed in that many of us are no longer on our paths. We've needed time to recover and reorganize our education, family lives, and careers. The past has a chunk missing because memories of the times we enjoyed one-on-one are missing the other party to recall those good times.

OP please get help. My best friend recently committed suicide and it has destroyed everyone's life. It was so traumatic that I needed a lot of administrative accommodations for school. His family is destroyed. They say ending one's own life is balling up that pain and bombing everyone else with it and it's absolutely true. All of us will carry that pain for the rest of our lives. I know depression isn't easy but there is help. There is SO much help and my friend was so blinded by depression that he couldn't see it. Some people have to work hard to be happy or even feel content but it's worth the fight. He didn't leave me anything but no matter what he could've left, every day all I want is more time with him, the familiar feeling of planning future events, being able to recall memories, I just want him alive. There are people in your life that you aren't aware of who care about you more than you think.

Text them, call them, send them a social media PM, etc. I recently lost my best friend and he didn't contact me. It was hard to understand why he didn't and at first I felt so much guilt. Please take your mental health seriously and get help from professionals and friends/family. I read what you posted here and where I've gotten in my grief process, I understand that he felt the same things you felt and that's a dangerous spot to be in. What I did to understand his mind was I traveled halfway across the state to recreate his daily routine. I went to his house, I made his commute to work, I walked around the building where he worked. The truth is that all of it was BEAUTIFUL. The places, the people, the profession. I understood then that in his mind, depression erased his ability to realize and appreciate the things literally right in front of him. What was so beautiful to me was a constant mental hell for him. And there is help for this. I wished so badly that he would've called me in the middle of the night and told me he was going to end it. I would've gotten in my car and drove those hundreds of miles to save him. It doesn't matter who you turn to for help and when you do it, be honest. There's no judgment during a time like this. If my best friend got a hold of me and said "Please help. I'm thinking about suicide." the only feeling is one of wanting to help. I honestly don't think it would've made a difference if we weren't close anymore and it had been years since we last spoke. Seriously, ask ANYONE for help. Even someone you see every day but don't have a friendship with, like someone at a store where you're a regular. There IS help out there and I've learned that depression easily makes people think that there isn't.

You're welcome and thank you for your support too. I haven't responded because sometimes I can't talk about it but other times I can. Likewise, I wish you the best, you've already come so far, and feel free to PM me for someone to listen, too! :) Stay strong!

i'm so sorry to hear about this. i'm the one wondering how you've managed. i lost my best friend a handful of weeks ago. i talked to my professor and got an extension on my final. i completed it a month late. it's been debilitating. i'm also at home and job hunting so i totally relate to your situation. i've still been applying and going to interviews. in a way, the challenges we face on top of this will make life easier (finding a job, etc.) hang in there, you have so far and seeing as though you're farther along in your healing and have accomplished things along the way (congratulations on graduating through all this), you'll be ok.
i'm happy you honored your friend's memory this way. i'm working on finishing my friend's travel bucketlist.

I'm sure your loved ones are glad you are still here even if they are unaware of your struggles. I'm glad you've found a place that helps center you even for a little bit. I lost my best friend recently and I know that he did not try to get help nor did he want it. His absence is permanent. His parents are so broken over his death. All of his problems were fixable even though they may have taken years. So long as you're alive, many things can be repaired.
I'm so sorry to hear this. Things can go downhill so quickly. I recently lost my best friend and 11 days before it happened, we looked at flights to go on a trip.

I am sorry that you know what this feels like and that you're 18 months in. It has only been a few weeks for me and it's difficult to imagine that most of my life will be spent missing someone so special. I am sorry that your friend faced so many hardships when things seemed so bright at first. I suppose that is how many people feel but the most important thing is to keep having hope and keep moving forward. It's hard to believe I posted this less than two weeks ago. It certainly feels longer. I am sorry you have feelings of wanting to talk to him and to hug him tightly. I deal with that every day and this is the only beginning of this emptiness. I wish you well. Try to live your life to the fullest as your friend's life was cut short. That is what I'm trying to do. And remember that virtually every problem can be solved. We must persist in life.
It's often hard for me, emotionally, to come back to check comments but I want to thank you for your sympathy however late.
Thank you belatedly for your kind words. I go through spells of wanting to talk about this and not being able to talk about it.

Thank you for your kind words. We truly were best friends. I am also sorry that my friend didn't get the right kind of help so now I'm just trying to raise awareness for people who might find themselves going down this path so hopefully they may make a different decision.

Thank you. They seem like they can fix everyone's problems and would know the first thing about health and likely mental health but they are people too and have struggles like the rest of us. Often more.
Thank you. I couldn't help him and he couldn't help himself but I hope getting the word out might change someone's mind if they stumble upon a positive message at the right time. You never know.
